<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|222|THE GOSPEL|CHA. III.}}</noinclude>to worke miracles: not doubting but he would begin a litle before his ordinary time for her sake, as S. Cyril thinketh he did: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''li. 2 in Io. c. 23''.}}and therfore she admonisheth the waiters to marke wel, & to execute whatsoeuer Christ should bid them doe.

''15. Cast them out.'') By this chastising corporally the defilers and abusers of the Temple he doth not onely shew his power, that being but one poore man he could by force execute his pleasure vpon so many sturdy fellowes: but also his soueraine authoritie ouer al offenders, and that not vpon their soules onely, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Profaners of Gods Church are to be punished in soul & body by the Spiritual power.}}as by excommunication and spiritual penalties, but so far as is requisite for the execution of spiritual iurisdiction, vpon their bodies and goods also. That the Spiritualtie may learne, how far and in what cases, for iust zeale of Christs Church, they may vse and exercise both spiritually and temporally their forces and faculties against offenders, specially against the prophaners of Gods Church, according to the Apostles allusion 1 Cor. 3. ''If any defile the Temple of God, him wil God destroy''.

''24. {{sc|Iesvs}} committed not him self.'') S. Augustine applieth this their first faith and beleefe in Christ, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Tract. in Io. 11''.}}sodenly raised vpon the admiration of his wonders, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The B. Sacrament is not to be giuen to nouices or yonglings in faith.}}but yet not fully formed or established in them, vnto the faith of Nouices or Catechumens in the Church: and Christs not committing his Person to them as yet, to the Churches like warinesse and wisedom, in not opening nor giuing to them our Lord in the B. Sacrament, because al were not to be trusted with that high point without ful trial of their faith.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. III.}}}}}}

{{c|''He teacheth Nicodemus, that to come to the kingdom of God, Baptisme is necessarie, as being our Regeneration. 10 Which point Nicodemus as then not vnderstāding, 11 he sheweth that they must beleeue him, and vvhat good cause there is for them so to doe. 23. After this he also baptizeth, and Iohn likewise at the same time. 25 Wherevpon a question being moued, Whether Baptisme is better, 25 Iohn ansvvereth it by saying, that he is so far inferiour to Christ, as a mere man to God most high.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, a bearded man.png|imgsize=115px|fl={{verse|chapter=3|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Holy Roode day, Maij 3.}}there vvas a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a prince of the Ievves. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=2}}† This man came to {{sc|Iesvs}} by night, and said to him, Rabbi, vve knovv that thou art come from God a maister, for no man can doe these signes vvhich thou doest, vnles God be vvith him. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=3}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to him, Amen, Amen I say to thee, Vnles a man be borne againe, he can not see the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}}† Nicodemus said to him, Hovv can a man be borne, vvhen he is old? can he enter into his mothers vvombe againe and be borne? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, Amen, Amen I say to thee, Vnles a man be {{sup|‖}} borne againe of vvater and the Spirit, he can not enter into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}}† That vvhich is borne of the flesh, is flesh: & that vvhich is borne of the spirit, is spirit. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}}† Marueil not, that I said to thee, You must be borne againe. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}}† The spirit breatheth vvhere {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We folow rather S. August. & those ancient fathers, which most commōly vnderstand this place of the holy Ghost, & not of the winde: although both senses be good.}}∷ he vvil: and thou hearest his voice, but thou knovvest not vvhence he commeth and vvhither he goeth: so is euery one that is borne of the Spirit. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}}† Nicodemus ansvvered, & said to him, Hovv can these things be done? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, and said to him, Thou art a<noinclude>{{rh|||maister}}</noinclude>
